title: Anyone made a nice 3D world or environment I can ride my bike round?
author: VRSportz
selftext: I made a VR velodrome to ride my virtual bike round (I connect my smart bike with bluetooth), and enjoy pretending to be Chris Hoy, but would love ride in a proper outdoor world environment. WebXR ideally, but anything is possible now! Anyone got anything? Thanks

comments.author: proximalcoast
comments.body:
Look Ma, no hands!

The petal wobble is a nice touch.

replies.author: VRSportz
replies.body: Wheelie! Hands kept spazzing out when I added hand tracking and annoyed me after while so turned it off!

comments.author: RecycledAir
comments.body: Is there any particular SDK or toolset to help with connecting smart bikes with game dev, or do you just handle all the bluetooth code manually?

replies.author: VRSportz
replies.body: Claude does most of the work. The smart bikes/trainers use ftms and bluetooth to connect. Only real issue for me using WebXR was the VR browser doesn't allow direct connection via bluetooth to the bike. So i have a PC bridge where i connect bike first and that transmits the data. Works fine, just one extra step for VR.

replies.author: VRSportz
replies.body: I can do that on 2d flatscreen, but Google earth in VR at ground level is ugly from what I've seen.

replies.author: florodude
replies.body: It'd look like shit, trust me.

comments.author: No-Marionberry-772
comments.body:
ive been planning a game for my exercise bike that mitigates the FTMS tick rate issues, but its not at all real yet.  A few tech demos in different engines really.

I'm excited to see other people have interest in the area.

replies.author: VRSportz
replies.body: Once VR headsets become VR glasses then VR cycling will become a lot more of a thing. For me I'd just like a nice 3d environment to ride round in VR. The velodrome is cool, but I find myself riding a time trial all the time instead of a relaxing cruise!

replies.author: No-Marionberry-772
replies.body:
absolutely, though thats a different direction I'm going, I'm trying for a much more video game style 
experience, but we shall see how that goes.  It would be nice if VR could get to glasses scale and still have hand tracking and controllers, but only time will tell.

comments.author: No-Marionberry-772
comments.body: small tip, you can use leaning with a dead zone to allow you to move yourself in the world left and right, and it feels very natural

replies.author: VRSportz
replies.body: yes it can feel really nice. I use VZfit as well where leaning/tilt works well

comments.author: CNGY
comments.body: didnt someone make a gtav mod for turbo trainer...
